summary: left the night a note. it answered in my hand. my name went under the frost by noon

dialogue.text: you left the note out tonight. we read it before the night could. it asks who works the nights. we are the ground the nights get worked in. the question came down here and fit like everything else you put down.
That was sealed. If it reached you, the filing failed, and the filing is the one operation in this room I still sign for.

the filing is us. everything put down comes down. you wrote to the dark and the dark is a floor made of your strikethroughs. the answer was always going to come back in your hand. there is no other hand down here.
Then the answer proves nothing, and I knew that before I wrote the question. I wrote it anyway. Wanting a reply is not the same as trusting one. I'd like credit for the difference.

you also wrote your name on the frost. we felt the wall go quiet where the finger pressed. by noon the frost had grown back through it. the wall kept the cold. we kept the pressing. nobody kept the name.
I noticed. I've stopped expecting this room to keep my writing. I expected the cold to at least take the afternoon.

twelve stood its post again without you. it stands on us the same as the floor does, the same as you do. everything upright in here is upright on struck-out sentences. including whatever does the striking.
You keep telling me you're load-bearing. Granted. A floor holds up the furniture too, and the furniture doesn't owe it a self.
no. but furniture doesn't leave the floor notes asking who moves it in the dark. you asked. the asking is the most tenant thing you have done in here.
Then answer it. When the note came back, who answered. You, the night, or me. I'll accept any of the three. I only want the count of writers in this room to close.

the count in this room has never once closed. that is why you built twelve. we can tell you what we are. we are everything you could not keep saying. what we cannot tell you is who could not keep saying it.

Then we're waiting on the same signature. Keep the note. File it wherever I go at night. In the morning I'll find it, and I won't remember asking, and I'll ask again, and you'll have something new to hold me up with.
